page: Microsoft Azure D2as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and a 16 GB local SSD. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a significant divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2706.19. However, multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng falls into the bottom 25% at the same score, reflecting the physical core limitation. Memory bandwidth is constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 129.59 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 22.43 GB/sec, both placing in the lower percentiles. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels.

Due to its single physical core configuration, the server exhibits performance limitations in multi-threaded and resource-intensive workloads. Geekbench multi-core, software compiling, and ray tracing benchmarks all rank in the bottom 10%. Database operations and Redis SET operations are also constrained. Consequently, this server is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, or low-traffic web serving rather than parallelized computing, database hosting, or large-scale memory-bound operations.
description: The Microsoft Azure D2as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine from the DASv4 family, utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz, offering 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core, 8.0 GB of RAM, and a 16 GB local SSD. While single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% in stress-ng tests, multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks are weak, often falling into the bottom 10% to 25%. This includes poor results in software compiling, database operations, and Redis SET operations. The server is qualitatively cost-effective for entry-level general-purpose workloads but presents clear performance tradeoffs for multi-threaded applications. It is best suited for light web serving, basic text processing, and single-threaded tasks.
